title: Waterwheel
prompt: A labelled bench adaptation of the page 32 overshot waterwheel has an elevated water reservoir, a controllable chute, a vertical wheel and a catch tray. Open flow sends water onto the upper rim and turns the horizontal shaft. Apply load couples that shaft to a small rope drum and hanging test mass, so available water power lifts the mass. Reduce flow compares the loaded response. Water drains into the tray. The lifting attachment and flow control are teaching fixtures. See-through shows the rim paddles or buckets, drainage path, hub, shaft, supports and attached load drum. Refill is an external reset and no self-powered water loop is implied.
blurb: A bench teaching adaptation of an overshot waterwheel uses finite gravity-fed water to turn a shaft and lift a test mass.

identity.note: The Wheel and Axle at Work / Waterwheel / Overshot Waterwheel, page 32 in both editions.
identity.mechanism: Water reaches the upper rim of a vertical wheel, acts on its paddles or buckets and drains as the wheel turns. The wheel transmits torque to its horizontal central shaft.
identity.classificationNote: Only The Wheel and Axle and Gears and Belts are main principle chapters in this unit. Other entries are named examples, diagrams or subsection headings. Greek Mill has both historical context and a named mechanism diagram.

adaptationDecision.reason: Retain as the vertical overshot wheel. Greek mill uses a horizontal rotor and vertical axle. Francis turbine guides enclosed water flow through a curved runner and drives a generator.
adaptationDecision.boundary: Catalog and figure metadata establish intended scope only. No existing figure runtime was certified.

prompt.note: The overshot wheel and load lesson are faithful adaptations. A recirculating display needs external pump energy and must not imply that the wheel powers an endless loop. Use a gravity-fed reservoir and catch tray for the smallest clear apparatus.
prompt.apparatusRelation: Named wheel with a labelled test load and water-supply fixture. The book supports rim-to-shaft force transmission, not this complete bench installation.

builderTruthNotes: Simple wheel assembly and teaching fixture. Label real paddles or buckets, rim, hub, shaft, supports, chute, reservoir, tray and test load if drawn. No quota-driven gearing.

Label all meaningful drawn real components and physical features. Distinguish force and travel overlays from anatomy. The individual builder brief must declare its expected minimum before building. No invented parts to meet a quota.
Identify the teaching adaptation in metadata, blurb and truth notes. Reset, specimen exchange, slow view and hand positioning are teaching controls rather than hidden machine hardware.

teachingFixtures: Coupling, rope drum and 0.5 kg test mass
External refill and manual load reset

model.description: Quasi-static power-limited model. No stored kinetic energy. Water in flight has negligible inventory. Reservoir plus tray remains 6 L.

truthNotes: 1988 access restricted and unverified. No edition union claimed.
The whole bench installation is an adaptation. The source supports rim-to-shaft force transmission.
Water drains only to the tray. Refill is external and lowers the mass by hand.
Static bearing friction holds this small load when stopped. Reduced flow can stall it.
Water films are illustrative. This is not a calibrated transient bucket simulation.
